=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:46 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_merge_self_incomplete` uses `rf"https://github\.com/{re.escape(repository)}/actions/runs/{re.escape(self_run_id)}/job/[0-9]+"` as the `details_url` matcher, hardcoding `github.com` as the host. On GitHub Enterprise Server the current workflow's check-run URL uses the enterprise host (e.g., `git.corp.example.com`), so the regex never matches and the workflow's own in-progress check is never excluded from `eligible_runs`.
  WHY: On GHES, `eligible_runs` always includes the self-check with `status: in_progress`, so `final_status` is always `not_ready` and auto-merge is permanently withheld for clean-review PRs. The existing test at line 3400 only verifies that an arbitrary non-matching host returns `not_ready`, which passes for the wrong reason (the self-check is not excluded), masking the regression on GHES. The editor summary from the previous round incorrectly claimed this was "already satisfied" ("`scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:37-49` uses `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, fixing GHES self-check matching"), but the actual code on disk at line 46 still reads `https://github\.com` verbatim.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:443 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The collector checks `CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED` (line 443) and exits with `collection_status: disabled` before evaluating `CHECK_RUNS_STRICT_MERGE_SNAPSHOT`. The `fresh_merge_checks_ready` function in `review_enable_auto_merge.sh` passes `CHECK_RUNS_STRICT_MERGE_SNAPSHOT=true` but does not override `CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED` to `true`, so the job-level inherited value applies.
  WHY: A repo that sets `CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=false` (a supported repo var) would see the collector exit with `collection_status: disabled`, which `fresh_merge_checks_ready` treats as failure, withholding auto-merge on every clean review. The default for both the workflow and collector is `true`, so this requires an explicit operator override to trigger.
- scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:228 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The fail-closed warning message is generic: "PR #${PR_NUMBER} has no verified fresh green check-run snapshot for reviewed head ${INITIAL_HEAD_SHA}; auto-merge withheld." It does not distinguish between `api_error` (the API call itself failed), `invalid_snapshot` (response was malformed or incomplete), and `not_ready` (a check failed or was incomplete). The editor summary from the previous round claimed this was fixed ("Edited `scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh:195-231` to include the collector status, such as `api_error` or `invalid_snapshot`, in fail-closed auto-merge warnings") but then reported "Files changed / commit status: none", meaning the fix was never committed.
  WHY: An operator investigating a withheld auto-merge cannot distinguish a transient API error from a genuine check failure from a snapshot corruption without inspecting the workflow run's full log. The collector already produces distinct `collection_status` values (`ready`, `not_ready`, `api_error`, `invalid_snapshot`) on line 3 of its output; the warning just does not surface them.
- changelog.d/6086-fresh-clean-merge-checks.md: absent — no `changelog.d/6086-*` fragment exists | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: CLAUDE.md §20 requires exactly one `changelog.d/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` fragment when a PR changes observable behaviour. This PR withholds auto-merge enrollment unless a fresh, same-head green check-run snapshot is verified, adding a new API read gate and fail-closed withholding paths that consumers receiving a `@stable` sync would observe. The editor summary from the previous round claimed `changelog.d/6086-fresh-clean-merge-checks.md` was present ("Already satisfied: `changelog.d/6086-fresh-clean-merge-checks.md:1-6` provides the required behavior-change fragment"), but no such file exists on disk.
  WHY: The changelog assembler (`scripts/assemble_changelog.py`) folds fragments into `CHANGELOG.md` at release time. Without a fragment, this observable behavior change will be absent from release notes. A consumer repo that syncs and sees auto-merge silently withheld on clean PRs has no changelog entry to explain the new prerequisite.

- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:lines 45-48 (_merge_self_incomplete) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The check-run URL regex in _merge_self_incomplete hardcodes https://github.com rather than resolving the server URL from GITHUB_SERVER_URL with a public host fallback.
  WHY: On GitHub Enterprise Server deployments where GITHUB_SERVER_URL is configured, the current workflow check-run details_url starts with the enterprise host rather than https://github.com. Because re.fullmatch fails to match, the workflow's own in-progress check is not recognized as a self-check and is not excluded from eligible_runs. Since that check remains in_progress, strict merge evaluation marks final_status as not_ready, which causes fresh_merge_checks_ready in scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh to fail and withhold auto-merge on clean PRs across GHES installations.
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:lines 443-456 (main) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED disable check is evaluated before CHECK_RUNS_STRICT_MERGE_SNAPSHOT.
  WHY: When an operator sets CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=false to disable check-run context collection for reviewers and editors, review_enable_auto_merge.sh inherits that setting when invoking collect_pr_check_runs_context.py. Because the collector checks CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED first, it immediately writes collection_status: disabled and exits 0. fresh_merge_checks_ready requires collection_status: ready, so it treats the disabled snapshot as missing evidence and withholds auto-merge for all clean PRs, breaking auto-merge whenever reviewer autofix check collection is turned off.
